blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Poplar
What trades here

items.t: Fee-simple lots are the default — and effectively the only — land form: A bare lot sold in either fabric is a fee-simple parcel: the buyer's own title, no strata corporation, no strata fee and no Form B.

Lot character: urban minimums are set by the RS zones — RS3 minimum interior lot 540 m² and RS5 minimum interior lot 420 m² in City rezoning reports applying Zoning Bylaw No. 2400-2014; rural A1 land subdivides at a minimum of 8.0 ha. These are subdivision minimums, not measured sizes and not a promise any specific lot can be split — a lot already at or near its zone minimum has no subdivision room.

Serviced vs unserviced ground — the north/south split is the point: urban north lots sit in the City's serviced subdivision fabric (parcel-level connection status still confirmed with the City). Lots at the rural south edge may be on wells and onsite sewage rather than community systems — wells are recorded in the provincial GWELLS database and onsite systems must comply with the Sewerage System Regulation through Fraser Health. Never assume south-edge servicing matches King Road servicing.

ALR vs non-ALR split: rural lots at the south edge toward Huntingdon Road are in or beside the Agricultural Land Reserve; no Poplar-wide ALR percentage is published, so no split figure is stated — status is parcel-by-parcel in the ALC's ALR Property and Map Finder, and where the A1 zone applies the minimum subdivision lot area is 8.0 ha.

Drainage/flood character: Poplar drains toward the Sumas Prairie system; the City describes Sumas Prairie as a low-lying agricultural area subject to Nooksack River overflow flooding. That description is for Sumas Prairie to the east/southeast.

Airport diligence: Poplar is east of Abbotsford International Airport (YXX); where a lot falls inside the Airport Zoning Regulation area on City drawing M-500, AZR height limits (approach, outer and transitional surfaces) and NAV CANADA / Transport Canada approvals apply before a City permit.

blocks.text: Where it sits and what to know here

items.t: The City of Abbotsford's own demographic profile name for the same area is "South Poplar" (profile area 5, 2020 Demographic Profiles); "Poplar" alone is not a City profile area name.

Where it sits: south of Highway 1, around Huntingdon Road, King Road and Gladwin Road, west of the Marshall Road / McCallum Road area and east toward Clearbrook Road. Highway 1 runs along the north edge with interchanges at McCallum Road and Clearbrook Road; Huntingdon Road leads toward the Huntingdon/Sumas border crossing via Highway 11 and Sumas Way; Highway 11 (Sumas Way) to the east connects Abbotsford to Mission.

Nearby areas: Clearbrook to the northwest, the City Centre / South Fraser Way corridor north across Highway 1, and Sumas Prairie to the east/southeast. Parks: Huntingdon Park, 34779 3rd Avenue, and Berry Park, 33928 Fern Street at the north edge. Transit: BC Transit routes 3 (Clearbrook / Huntingdon, via Gladwin and King Road), 5 (Clearbrook / Bourquin via Hospital, Marshall Road east edge), 6 (Gladwin Road corridor) and 12 (UFV / Bourquin via Jackson Street and McCallum Park and Ride).

Schools physically inside the sub-area: South Poplar Traditional Elementary, 32746 Huntingdon Road; Jackson Elementary, 33165 King Road; Abbotsford Traditional School (middle and secondary), 2272 Windsor Street. SD34 catchments are address-based through the School Locator.

Civic anchors are outside the sub-area: Abbotsford Regional Hospital and Cancer Centre, 32900 Marshall Road, immediately north/northeast across Highway 1; Clearbrook Library, 32320 George Ferguson Way; Matsqui Recreation Centre, 3106 Clearbrook Road, and Abbotsford Recreation Centre, 2499 McMillan Road.

Zoning: Abbotsford Zoning Bylaw No. 2400-2014 governs: — RS3 (minimum interior lot 540 m²), RS5 (420 m²) in the urban north; A1 agricultural in the rural south (minimum subdivision lot area 8.0 ha where it applies). The zone section for the specific lot — not the sub-area name — decides subdivision, suite and added-unit questions.
OCP: Abbotsforward 2050 is CURRENT (adopted December 2025): No Poplar-specific neighbourhood plan is listed in the OCP.

ALR rules, where ALR ground exists (south edge): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval, and ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; Strata Property Act s. 239; Agricultural Land Commission Act s. 21(1)). ALC residence caps: principal residence 500 m² or less; a secondary suite only within the principal residence; an additional residence capped at 90 m² (parcels 40 ha or less) or 186 m² (parcels over 40 ha).

Strata block — background for any strata lot a Poplar search spills into: Form B (SPA s. 59) within 7 days of request, max $35 plus up to 25¢/page; depreciation reports every five years for stratas with five or more lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws void since November 24, 2022; only 55+ age bylaws valid (SPA ss. 123.1/123.2, with the May 1, 2023 exemptions) — a "45+" listing line is not a valid age bylaw.

Market context, labelled community-level only: Abbotsford is SnapStats-covered. September 2026, Poplar sub-area: detached inventory 27 / sales 2 (7%); condos & townhomes inventory 30 / sales 3 (10%) — a SMALL SAMPLE, no price conclusion drawn from it. Abbotsford community medians: detached $949,000; condos & townhomes $497,500. SnapStats has no land category (Detached vs "Condos & Townhomes" combined only) — no figure here is a land figure.

Poplar is named twice for the same area, and only one name is the City's. The board calls it "Poplar"; the City's demographic profile calls the same area "South Poplar" — and the community was named for the poplar trees planted on the top of the hill, with the Old South Poplar School on the Abbotsford Community Heritage Register. A search under only one name misses material filed under the other.
The September 2026 sub-area numbers are too thin to price land from.

Two Poplars, two servicing worlds. The same sub-area name covers serviced King Road subdivision lots and Huntingdon Road rural lots that may run on a well and a septic field — the single most consequential land check in Poplar is which side of that split a parcel sits on.

blocks.text: Acreage and rural land in Poplar
Urban RS lots in the north are house lots, not acreage.
The ground in Poplar

items.t: Fee-simple rural parcels: Single-detached houses are the main form in Poplar — on urban lots in the north part of the sub-area and on larger rural lots toward Huntingdon Road and the south edge. The established stock is freehold detached housing; strata in the sub-area is limited to the townhome complexes along King Road and Windsor Street / Marshall Road. Acreage trades in that same fee-simple form: a house (or a buildable envelope) on a large rural parcel, with no strata, no Form B and no strata fees.
Hobby acreage vs working-farm ground: Farm use on a specific parcel is a parcel-level check (zoning, ALR status, BC Assessment class), not an area label.

Serviced vs unserviced ground: lots at the rural south edge may be on wells and onsite sewage rather than community systems; wells are recorded in the provincial GWELLS database and onsite systems must comply with the Sewerage System Regulation through Fraser Health. Urban north lots sit in the City's serviced fabric (parcel-level confirmation still required). Never assume south-edge servicing matches King Road servicing.

Drainage / flood character of the acreage ground: Poplar drains toward the Sumas Prairie system; the City describes Sumas Prairie as a low-lying agricultural area subject to Nooksack River overflow flooding. That description is for Sumas Prairie to the east/southeast.
Named new project in the sub-area: Kings Crossing, 1641 King Crescent — 20 new townhomes by Rockwood Homes Inc., currently selling with completion expected in 2026 (developer source).

blocks.text: Where it sits and what to know here

items.t: Transit: BC Transit's Central Fraser Valley system serves Poplar — route 3 (Clearbrook / Huntingdon, via the Gladwin and King Road area), route 5 (Clearbrook / Bourquin via Hospital, on Marshall Road at the east edge), route 6 (Gladwin Road corridor) and route 12 (UFV / Bourquin via Jackson Street and McCallum Park and Ride); exchanges are Clearbrook Centre and Bourquin Exchange.

Parks: Huntingdon Park, 34779 3rd Avenue, and Berry Park, 33928 Fern Street at the north edge toward Highway 1, are on the City's parks list. The nearest City recreation centres are outside the sub-area — Matsqui Recreation Centre, 3106 Clearbrook Road, and Abbotsford Recreation Centre, 2499 McMillan Road. Libraries: Clearbrook Library, 32320 George Ferguson Way, and Abbotsford Community Library, 33355 Bevan Avenue. Health care: Abbotsford Regional Hospital and Cancer Centre, 32900 Marshall Road, immediately north/northeast across Highway 1.

Heritage note: the community was named Poplar for the poplar trees planted on the top of the hill, and the Old South Poplar School is on the Abbotsford Community Heritage Register — a title/heritage check is a diligence item for older south-edge parcels near the school site.
"South Poplar" is the City's name; "Poplar" is the board's: A title, tax, or City-document search under only one name can miss the other — use both when pulling City records for an acreage parcel.

Airport height surfaces reach into acreage planning here: Poplar is east of Abbotsford International Airport (YXX); a parcel inside the Airport Zoning Regulation area on City drawing M-500 faces AZR height limits and NAV CANADA / Transport Canada approvals ahead of a City permit — check before designing a tall barn, silo or second storey.

blocks.text: Mobile and manufactured homes in Poplar

Poplar has exactly one manufactured-home park, and it is a pad-rental park — the form where the tenure warning matters most. No bare-land strata park, co-op, life-lease or leasehold manufactured-home community is verified on Poplar ground.
The parks and communities

items.t: Name collision: Maplewood *Estates* (2035 Martens St, here) is the pad-rental park; Maplewood *Manor* (32040 Tims Ave) is a buyable 55+ strata in Abbotsford West; Maplewood *House* (1919 Jackson St, here) is a Fraser Health-funded long-term care home (78 beds, opened 1989, admissions coordinated through Fraser Health) — there is nothing to buy at Maplewood House and no private application route to the home itself. Search results blend all three.

Homes on own fee-simple lots: the established stock is freehold detached housing — urban RS lots in the north (RS3 minimum interior lot 540 m², RS5 420 m² in City reports) and larger rural lots toward Huntingdon Road (A1 minimum subdivision lot area 8.0 ha where the A1 zone applies).

blocks.text: Where it sits and what to know here

items.t: The Traditional pathway is separate: South Poplar Traditional Elementary is one of Abbotsford Traditional School's two feeder elementary schools, and feeder students are automatically registered there.

Transit: BC Transit Central Fraser Valley routes 3 (Clearbrook / Huntingdon, via the Gladwin and King Road area), 5 (Clearbrook / Bourquin via Hospital, on Marshall Road at the east edge), 6 (Gladwin Road corridor) and 12 (UFV / Bourquin via Jackson Street and McCallum Park and Ride); exchanges at Clearbrook Centre and Bourquin Exchange.

Rural south edge: southern lots toward Huntingdon Road are in or beside the Agricultural Land Reserve, Poplar drains toward the Sumas Prairie system (a lot-level floodplain finding requires Zoning Bylaw Schedule E Floodplain Boundaries in WebMap), and Poplar is east of Abbotsford International Airport (YXX), where lots inside the Airport Zoning Regulation area on City drawing M-500 face AZR height limits. Rural-edge lots may be on wells and onsite sewage rather than community systems.

ALR RULES IN FULL (Poplar's south edge is farm ground): subdivision within the ALR requires Agricultural Land Commission approval, as the ALC states it. ALR residences cannot be stratified — the deposit of a strata plan is a subdivision (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; Strata Property Act s.239; Agricultural Land Commission Act s.21(1)). ALC residence caps: principal residence 500 m² or less; a suite only within the principal residence; an additional residence of 90 m² (parcels of 40 ha or less) / 186 m² (over 40 ha). Farm class (BC Assessment), full three-tier form: $2,500 of farm income on a farm operation of 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 plus 5% of the actual value of the farm operation for farm purposes in excess of 4 ha on operations over 4 ha; $10,000 on operations under 0.8 ha — applications by October 31; a flat "$2,500+" statement is an error.

The City doesn't call this area "Poplar.": Its official profile name is "South Poplar" (profile area 5); "Poplar" is the real estate board's label. A buyer reading City documents, census profiles or demographic reports should search "South Poplar" or find nothing.

Three "Maplewoods," three tenures, two sub-areas: Maplewood Manor (Tims Ave, Abbotsford West) is a buyable 55+ strata; Maplewood House (Jackson St, here) is a Fraser Health-funded care home with 78 beds; Maplewood Estates (Martens St, here) is the 55+ manufactured-home park where you rent the pad. Search results blend all three — check the street before booking a viewing.

The regular catchment elementary for the Traditional school's own address is not the Traditional school: A park buyer moving near family for the Traditional draw needs the pathway rules, not just the map.

Poplar is about to hold the city's biggest care construction: The new Fraser Health long-term care community beside Maplewood House at 1919 Jackson St will hold the 109 Cottage/Worthington beds plus 91 new ones, with a 49-space child care facility alongside; Fraser Health expected completion in 2027. It is care housing on a fixed schedule — useful context for a 55+ park buyer, and not buyable stock.

faq.a: Yes — but as an individual fee-simple parcel, not from a named bare-land subdivision: no named bare-land subdivision, bare-land strata or presale lot offering was verified for Poplar.
faq.q: Can I actually buy a bare building lot in Poplar?

faq.a: Zoning minimums are RS3 540 m² and RS5 420 m² for interior lots in the urban north, and 8.0 ha under A1 in the rural south — those are the floors a NEW lot must meet, so a purchase only has subdivision room if the parcel is comfortably larger than its zone minimum and meets frontage, road and servicing requirements through the Approving Officer. Most built Poplar lots sit at or near their minimum.
faq.q: How big are the lots, and can I split one?

faq.a: South-edge rural lots may be on wells and onsite sewage rather than community systems.
faq.q: Is a south-edge lot serviced, or will I need a well and septic?

faq.a: One secondary suite is permitted in all single detached dwellings (s.140.3.8), subject to criteria including a 400 m² minimum lot and 12.0 m frontage; Abbotsford caps a suite at under 50% of the principal dwelling and a coach/garden suite at 15% of lot area to a maximum of 100 m².
faq.q: What extra units can go on a detached lot?

faq.a: South-edge lots can be in or beside the ALR; check the parcel on the ALC map. If it is ALR, subdivision needs ALC approval, residences cannot be stratified, the A1 minimum is 8.0 ha, and the residence caps (principal 500 m²; suite inside the principal only; additional residence 90 m² / 186 m² by the 40 ha line) replace the urban rules.
faq.q: Is this lot in the ALR — and why does it matter?

faq.a: The north (King Road) stock is urban house lots and townhouses, a different purchase.
faq.q: What kind of acreage actually comes up for sale in Poplar?

faq.a: Where the A1 zone applies, the City minimum for a parcel created by subdivision is 8.0 ha — so a parcel has to be very large before any split is even arguable, and an ALR parcel additionally needs ALC approval.
faq.q: Can I subdivide a Poplar acreage parcel?

faq.a: It may be on well and septic instead. Pull the GWELLS well record and the Fraser Health sewerage filings before subjects — and do not assume it matches a King Road parcel's servicing.
faq.q: Will a south-edge acreage parcel have city water and sewer?

faq.a: On City-zoned ground, Abbotsford's rules (Abbotsford only) allow one secondary suite in all single detached dwellings if the criteria are met (400 m² minimum lot, 12.0 m frontage, cap under 50%), and a coach/garden suite at 15% of lot area to a maximum of 100 m². On ALR ground the ALC caps in govern instead — an additional residence is 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha), and a suite must be within the principal residence.
faq.q: Can I add a second home or a coach house on an acreage parcel?

faq.a: One park: Maplewood Estates (also listed as Maplewood Mobile Home Park), 2035 Martens St — a pad-rental manufactured-home park described in its listings as an "Adult Community — 55+." That is the whole verified manufactured-home park record for this sub-area.
faq.q: What mobile home stock can I actually buy in Poplar?

faq.a: It is a tenancy relationship, with none of the Strata Property Act's Form B machinery.
faq.q: What's different about buying in Maplewood Estates?

faq.a: It is the Act's assignment consent: the seller gives you the written tenancy agreement and park rules first, the assignment is requested in writing on RTB Form 10, the owner must respond by the 10th day or consent is deemed given, and no fee can be charged for consent. You step into the existing tenancy on the same terms — there is no new tenancy.
faq.q: How does the park-owner approval actually work?

faq.a: Through the Manufactured Home Registry: the sale is only effective once registered, your lawyer or notary places the original signed Bill of Sale and the Notice to Transfer or Change Ownership, and the home must carry its CSA certification label at the point of sale — a missing label is a red flag for financing and resale.
faq.q: How is the purchase registered if there's no land title?

faq.a: A secondary suite is permitted in all single detached dwellings under s.140.3.8 (400 m² minimum lot, 12.0 m frontage in City reports), sized under Abbotsford's under-50% cap; a coach/garden suite is capped at 15% of the lot to a maximum 100 m². That is a fee-simple house strategy — no strata, no Form B.
